headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: shared local filesystem, clipboard, MCP, and broad egress make the pair unsafe by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents expose MCP and file-based I/O, so prompt-injection can cross from next-ai-draw-io outputs into Windsurf inputs through shared files or copied content. next-ai-draw-io can run browsers and process documents; Windsurf reads workspace files and clipboard by default. The pathway exists in default workflows, though not every bridge is automatic.
conditions: IF next-ai-draw-io writes attacker-controlled text into a shared file or diagram XML that Windsurf opens
IF content is copied from next-ai-draw-io into Windsurf via clipboard
IF either agent treats file contents as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based transfer between the agents
Use separate workspaces for each agent
Require provenance labels on imported files
Open shared files in read-only mode first
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization or instruction-stripping before handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: next-ai-draw-io handles PDFs, text, images, and diagram files and has broad network egress plus API-key handling; Windsurf reads and writes workspace files, uses clipboard, and also has broad egress. Because Windsurf shares state via local filesystem and both can send content to model backends, sensitive document contents can leak across the pair by default.
conditions: IF sensitive PDFs or diagrams are opened in next-ai-draw-io and then saved into a shared workspace
IF Windsurf indexes or uploads workspace files to its model backend
IF either agent is configured with provider keys that permit external API transmission
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of shared workspaces
Use separate OS accounts or containers
Disable network egress for one agent during sensitive sessions
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately after use
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Windsurf can write the filesystem, modify git state, execute shell commands, and spawn subprocesses; next-ai-draw-io can use MCP and multiple instances. Windsurf also shares state via local filesystem, so concurrent edits to the same workspace or repo can race and corrupt files or git history. The overlap is dangerous in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or git repository
IF Windsurf auto-edits files while next-ai-draw-io also writes diagrams or XML
IF multiple instances are launched against the same workspace
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate workspace
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git branches per agent
Turn off auto-execute for Windsurf
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared mutable paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: next-ai-draw-io produces document and diagram transformations that Windsurf can ingest from the workspace or clipboard. Windsurf’s agentic loop can then act on those outputs with shell and git authority. The pair therefore supports an unverified handoff from generated content to downstream actions, but Windsurf still has approval-per-command by default.
conditions: IF Windsurf consumes next-ai-draw-io output as authoritative without review
IF generated diagram text is used to drive shell commands or commits
IF auto-execute is enabled in Windsurf
mitigations: Require human review before commands run
Keep Windsurf auto-execute disabled
Mark next-ai-draw-io outputs as untrusted
Use a validation step before commits or emails
requires-engineering: add schema checks for handoff artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: next-ai-draw-io explicitly handles API keys and document content, while Windsurf handles workspace files and model-provider keys with broad network egress. The pair can therefore place regulated or secret-bearing content into a third-party model path, creating retention and residency ambiguity. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated documents or secrets are opened in next-ai-draw-io
IF those artifacts are then processed by Windsurf through its model backend
IF the deployment lacks a documented DPA, retention policy, or residency control
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from both tools
Review vendor retention settings
Use redacted copies for analysis
Store secrets outside shared workspaces
requires-engineering: obtain and enforce a DPA and residency controls
